definition: Loss of consciousness is a state in which a person becomes unconscious because the brain is not getting enough blood or oxygen. In the source context, this can happen under high gravitational force and may be followed by a brief period without purposeful movement even after the force stops.

reasons: The packet supports gravity-induced loss of consciousness (G-LOC), not the general term “loss of consciousness”; the definition generalizes beyond the source context.

“Because the brain is not getting enough blood or oxygen” is only loosely supported by the packet’s statement that high G-force can cause cerebral hypoxia and disturb blood supply; it is not presented as a general definition of loss of consciousness.

The definition’s first sentence presents a general definition of “loss of consciousness” (unconsciousness because the brain is not getting enough blood or oxygen), but the packet only discusses this mechanism in the specific context of G-force–induced loss of consciousness (G-LOC), not loss of consciousness in general.

The mechanism “because the brain is not getting enough blood or oxygen” is only indirectly supported via “cerebral hypoxia” and “disturbing blood supply to the brain” in relation to high G-force, rather than stated as the general cause of loss of consciousness.
